sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Ripresa, manager of a renowned orchestra in Nuova Volsinii. After observing that many of the city's power players have deep-rooted ties to Rhodes Island, she reached out to Rhodes Island of her own accord to seek a business partnership, hoping to raise her orchestra's profile. At her own request, she also takes part in some field operations.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
A small amount of Originium crystallization is visible on Operator Ripresa's thigh.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.25u/L
Operator Ripresa was infected with Oripathy as a child; her condition is currently stable.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
It was the fourth time Ripresa had pressed a new tape into his hands after piano class, and Czerny finally could not hold it in.
The first tape could still pass for homework—a piano etude. But the tapes that followed held a trombone solo, then an oboe and bassoon playing off each other, and this one, apparently, the entire percussion section performing together in a certain movement. Ripresa was extremely engaged in class, always able to draw wider conclusions from a single question, and she practiced diligently. Whenever the other students in the piano class mentioned her, they always said she had to be Mr. Czerny's number one fan. For a while, Czerny himself thought so too.
'Miss Liesel, is there something you want from me?'
'Uh, I... I've just always been really interested in your compositional methods, sir...'
'That is not what I am talking about. You have sat through enough of my lessons that you must know my style by now. And I now understand what makes the performances on those tapes distinctive—heh, I have to admit, your choice of repertoire is quite interesting as well. Out with it. What is it you actually want me to do?'
Ripresa froze for a few seconds, then pulled several videotapes out of the bag she carried.
'Mr. Czerny, these are all live recordings of the Black Velvet Curtain Orchestra. We're a small symphony orchestra of fewer than twenty people, and I'm the one conducting at the moment...'
Listening to Ripresa's pitch, Czerny fell into thought. He ran through his upcoming schedule, wondering whether he had time for a trip to Nuova Volsinii. An orchestra of Leithanians? He had no idea what sparks might fly between them and himself, a concert pianist. Ripresa was still going on at length when Czerny cleared his throat.
'I can work with your orchestra—'
'Wha—! Really?! Thank you, Mr. Czerny! Oh, right, about the style of the new piece—everyone in our orchestra agrees that something full of hope suits us better than something melancholy! With Mr. Czerny composing for us, that hope is sure to reach the audience's hearts through our performance!'
'...A new piece?'
Czerny was momentarily at a loss for words, forcing back down the offer he had yet to voice: 'to take charge of your orchestra's piano part as a guest performer.' Ripresa went on describing her request and her vision. The new piece she wanted was remarkably specific, and the character of those tapes was vivid enough that, little by little, a new melody began to take shape in Czerny's head.

Later, Czerny gave the Black Velvet Curtain Orchestra a piece tailored to them, and unsurprisingly, the new work's premiere was a resounding success in Nuova Volsinii. Afterward we did consider whether we ought to tell Operator Ripresa that on Rhodes Island we are all colleagues, that she can simply state any request directly, and that she need not fall back on the old methods she used to negotiate partnerships in Nuova Volsinii. But Operator Ripresa is always so full of energy when she goes about such things—she even seems to enjoy it. Perhaps there is nothing wrong with letting her keep to her old methods after all.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
While the Human Resources operator was running a background check on Operator Ripresa, some rather odd rumors were making the rounds. We asked Operator Bellone about the matter; he only smiled faintly, left us with the words 'She is good to her family,' and walked away.
After the musician Paula Meminger was murdered, the theater the Black Velvet Curtain Orchestra had long partnered with was sealed off for investigation. To keep rehearsals and performances on schedule, the orchestra had no choice but to rent other venues around Nuova Volsinii on a temporary basis and try to build new working relationships.
The arrangement with the new theater was at first limited to temporary rental. As rehearsals intensified, however, all manner of additional costs arose along the way. Continuing to treat it as a temporary rental meant the venue would have to absorb those losses alone; yet if the arrangement were terminated, the orchestra would struggle to find a comparable replacement venue on short notice. The two sides thus reached a standoff.
Ripresa did not shy away from the problems already in front of her. She checked the rehearsal records against the expense sheets one by one, laid out every additional cost explicitly, and, in her capacity as the orchestra's manager, voluntarily folded them into the orchestra's own accounts. It was not an easy decision. For an orchestra in the middle of upheaval, extra spending meant Ripresa would have to redistribute an already strained budget, and that she would have to shoulder the risk herself. Even so, Ripresa chose to take the cost back out of the venue's hands—if the partnership had broken down at that moment, what the orchestra stood to bear would have gone far beyond losses on paper.
In follow-up interviews, the Human Resources operator learned that the venue, too, had found Ripresa's decision rather unexpected.
This approach kept the partnership alive, and the two sides began renegotiating costs and scheduling. Whether it will ultimately grow into a stable, long-term partnership remains to be seen, but at the very least the immediate problem was properly resolved and did not escalate into conflict—just as with every other problem touching on the interests of Ripresa and her orchestra.
Even at the end of our investigation, we still could not put a clear definition on Ripresa's conduct. She does not appear to be expanding her influence so much as making a habit of standing in front of everyone and blocking whatever trouble is at hand. That is less the behavior of a mere manager than that of a...
'That little Caprinae stepped in like a godmother and settled the feud between those vicious foreigners and our famiglia!'
After entering all this information, the Human Resources operator in charge of the background check could not help thinking back to that rumor, heard at the very start of the investigation.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
During our visits to the Black Velvet Curtain Orchestra, its members repeatedly described a similar feeling: many of them have come to genuinely feel that they are 'people of Nuova Volsinii'—or rather, 'members of Nuova Volsinii's Black Velvet Curtain.'
Most of them fled Leithanien for Siracusa years ago. Their memories of Leithanien are mostly bitter, and they have always kept a wary attitude toward Siracusa as well. Even with a gift for music or Originium Arts, life in Siracusa's various cities did not go well for them, and many had at some point given up music altogether—after all, a movement that Leithanien would not accept was not thereby assured of flourishing in Siracusa. Only once Paula Meminger brought them together did they seem to find somewhere they could set down their feet, if only for a while.
Yet after Paula's death, what the orchestra faced was not only upheaval in personnel and venues, but a reexamination of where it was headed. Members recall that during that period they realized clearly, for the first time, that without a stable anchor they could scatter at any moment. For them, 'leaving' had always been a real option.
The change came after Ripresa took over every last piece of the orchestra's business.
She never tried to define an identity for the orchestra, nor did she stress to its members what they ought to represent. She simply kept pushing forward with work that looked trivial but was crucial: making sure rehearsals were not cancelled at short notice, confirming usage details with the venue over and over, drawing up contingency plans in advance to head off potential conflicts. As these arrangements gradually took hold, a subtle change occurred in the members' minds—a change that leaned toward putting down roots. When we asked what had caused it, their answers were not uniform, yet all pointed to the same thing: Liesel is here, and Liesel will be conducting them tomorrow.
It is worth noting that this sense of being 'people of Nuova Volsinii' did not come from the city explicitly accepting them, but from the orchestra itself. To its members, the 'Black Velvet Curtain' is no longer merely an organization that gathers performers, but a collective capable of holding a life. Within it, they need not explain their origins over and over, nor stay perpetually prepared for wherever they might have to go next.
The people whom Paula once brought together now have, under the leadership of her adopted daughter—perhaps for the first time since leaving Leithanien—a true 'home,' one that needs no repeated confirmation and will not easily be lost.

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
'The Caprinae who killed Mama Paula was sentenced in the end by Chief Justice Lavinia. I was sitting in the gallery. I watched that man just stand there without any expression at all, confessing to every last charge. Even if to him Mama Paula was only a stranger—only a symbol, even, a symbol that had no place in the story he believed in—for a long time after the trial ended I still felt the whole thing was absurd. I couldn't accept it.
'Mama Paula was never preaching some outrageous, treasonous idea the way the killer claimed—she never once gathered us together to oppose anything. From beginning to end, all Mama Paula ever told me and the other members of the orchestra was that we should speak the truth, that we shouldn't be afraid, and then enjoy music—enjoy the music we love. I don't understand... why it turned out this way. I don't understand, so I have to do something.
'Revenge? Ah, no! The case is closed, and the killer got the punishment he deserved. The orchestra members feel the same way I do about that. What I meant by "I have to do something" is really... maybe just stubbornness. I don't think Mama Paula did anything wrong, and neither did anyone in the orchestra, so I'm certainly not going to make everyone change the way they live just because it rubs somebody the wrong way. We'll live exactly like this on purpose, and we'll live even more freely than before. Let those people in Leithanien stew. We'll play the music we love no matter what—only the music we love!
'If what you're asking is whether I hate the killer... he took away the mother I loved most and wounded the hearts of my family, so of course I hate him. But... I won't let him, or anyone like him, ruin my life. I think that's what Mama Paula would have wanted, too.'

[Classified Log]
Grimmacht no longer makes a sound, the phantom of Gaul has appeared among the clouds, and Ewigegnade, now holding sole authority, has set about purging Leithanien of its dissonant notes—her heavy hand already reaching beyond Leithanien's borders. Under such circumstances, Rhodes Island must think carefully about its next move.

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Dear Mr. Czerny,
I hope this letter finds you well.
Please forgive me for not greeting you in person—I have been busy with the Black Velvet Curtain Orchestra's recent performances. I am writing this time to share a small change that has taken place in the orchestra, and to ask a favor of you.
Just as Mama Paula once met the uncles and aunts of the orchestra, yesterday I met a Caprinae carrying an instrument case with nowhere left to go. She said she had come from Leithanien to Nuova Volsinii as well. There was much in what she told me that I did not really understand, but I think there must still be many people like Mama Paula who cannot play the music they love in their own homeland. She listened to us rehearse the piece you wrote for our orchestra, and she said she loved it! So I have decided to let her stay, and to bring her into the Black Velvet Curtain Orchestra as our second violist.
By now you must already have guessed what my request is... Yes, the viola section was not short-handed to begin with, but I still want her to stay, and I want to make room within that work for a place that truly belongs to her.
That piece was written by you for our orchestra—I have never forgotten that, and it is precisely why I am reluctant to simply have her play alongside the other violist. If I did, her presence would feel forced, and the overall performance would no longer match your original artistic vision. I would much rather she be answered by this work in earnest, just like everyone else in the orchestra. But as you know, I am nowhere near as accomplished as Mama Paula, and I am still learning about composition...
And so I make this presumptuous request: could you help us revise the piece, so that the second violist carries a clear and distinctive meaning within it? Whether by reworking the part assignments, the musical form, or anything else you judge appropriate, I trust your judgment completely and entrust the matter to you with an easy mind.
The truth is, she still doesn't know that the orchestra members and I have decided to keep her. Before writing this letter I followed her in secret and saw her go into a music shop to ask about selling a secondhand instrument... Mr. Czerny, please! I'm so afraid she'll give up music! Until your reply comes, I'll find some way to get her performing together with us!
I look forward to your reply!
Liesel
